record.paper_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
record.original_question: How do existing underwater communication technologies behave under smart malicious nodes that can switch between passive and active attack modes on the fly, and how should security be analyzed when those malicious nodes are equipped with state-of-the-art capabilities such as multiple-input multiple-output operation, full duplex, GPUs, and the ability to launch attacks in both air and water media?

evidence.quote: A smart malicious node is a node that can assess the situation for launching attacks, for example a smart malicious node can be a node that can switch between passive and active modes on the fly [198, 199].
Therefore, an interesting problem is to analyze the existing state-of-the-art underwater communication technologies under smart malicious nodes.

In particular, it will be interesting to conduct such security analysis in the presence of malicious nodes equipped with the state-of-the-art machinery (i.e., Multiple Input and Multiple Output (MIMO), full duplex, GPUs capable of launching attacks in both mediums).
Additionally, to the best of our knowledge, a full-duplex malicious node is not considered in the literature.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an underwater or air-water wireless communication network consisting of legitimate transmitters and receivers that use one or more of the standard underwater channel modalities (acoustic, radio-frequency, optical/visible-light, and magnetic induction links), possibly combined with above-water radio links at the air-water interface. Introduce into this network one or more "smart malicious nodes" defined as follows: a smart malicious node can sense its local channel and traffic environment and adaptively switch, on the fly, between a passive attack mode (e.g., eavesdropping, traffic analysis) and an active attack mode (e.g., jamming, spoofing, message injection, replay, Sybil behavior). Each malicious node is additionally equipped with state-of-the-art capabilities: (i) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) transmission and reception with several antennas/transducers, (ii) full-duplex operation, allowing it to transmit and receive simultaneously on the same band, (iii) high-throughput GPU-based computation enabling real-time signal processing, machine-learning-based attack adaptation, and cryptanalytic effort, and (iv) the ability to operate and launch attacks in both the underwater medium and the air medium, exploiting the air-water interface.

Develop a rigorous security-analysis framework for such networks that:
1. Models the smart malicious node as a decision process that chooses, at each time step and based on observations, between passive and active modes so as to optimize an adversarial objective (e.g., maximize information leakage or disruption while minimizing detection probability).
2. Quantifies, for each existing state-of-the-art underwater communication technology (acoustic, RF, optical, magnetic induction, and hybrid air-water schemes), the achievable secrecy capacity, detection probability, outage probability, and throughput of the legitimate link in the presence of such adversaries, accounting for MIMO degrees of freedom, full-duplex self-interference cancellation, GPU-enabled adaptive attacks, and cross-medium attacks at the air-water boundary.
3. Determines necessary and sufficient conditions on system parameters (number of legitimate and adversarial antennas, transmit power, channel statistics, coding scheme, key-management protocol, etc.) under which secure and reliable communication is provably feasible against this adversary class, and identifies regimes in which no such guarantee is possible.

Provide the complete model, derive the corresponding performance and security bounds, and characterize defensive countermeasures that achieve those bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction in the underwater and air-water wireless communication security literature. A brief search does not reveal a comprehensive security analysis of state-of-the-art underwater technologies against smart malicious nodes that adaptively switch between passive and active modes while equipped with MIMO, full-duplex, GPU-based, and cross-medium capabilities; in particular, full-duplex underwater adversaries appear largely unstudied. The problem is therefore taken as open.

status_evidence.title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies smart malicious nodes and full-duplex underwater adversaries as open security problems.
status_evidence.claim: The security analysis of underwater communications against smart, MIMO/full-duplex/GPU-equipped, cross-medium malicious nodes is highlighted as an unresolved research direction.
